beats.idea: Purchasing power, gold backing, and legal status questioned
beats.shows: Note–rice arrow; gold? Payment tick versus law scroll?
beats.template_note: Buyer offers ₹100; shopkeeper gives rice. Gold appears with a question mark, then payment acceptance and a stamped law scroll appear separately with a question mark between them; do not imply equivalence.

beats.idea: Gold-backed notes could be redeemed for gold
beats.relation_note: Return note → bank receives note → bank gives gold → gold rests in the holder's hand; then contrast today's rupee.
beats.shows: Note enters bank; gold reaches hand; modern redemption crossed
beats.template_note: Gold redemption: holder returns one note; teller takes it and hands over gold labelled 1 gram. Hold gold visibly in the recipient's hand. On 'आज', reveal a modern rupee note; on 'नहीं', cross its redemption arrow to gold, not the note itself.

beats.idea: Paper has little material value; redemption gives value
beats.shows: Note exchanged for gold; receipt paired with goods
beats.template_note: Holder presents note; teller gives fixed gold on demand. Then contrast low-value paper with note-to-gold promise; pair receipt with claimable goods.

beats.idea: Gold reserves alone do not give holders claims
beats.shows: Identical gold vaults; only one note carries claim
beats.template_note: Gold पाने names a claim, not a completed redemption; compare reserves alone with reserves plus the holder’s claim.

beats.idea: Redemption promise explains the need for backing
beats.shows: Redemption promise points to new notes needing gold
beats.template_note: Forward-looking causal link, not an enacted note-issuing process; no reserve ratio specified.

beats.idea: One extra note needs one extra gram
beats.shows: Ten gold–note pairs; extra gram enables eleventh note
beats.template_note: Start with a question mark beside note eleven. At '10 grams', build ten gold units paired with ten notes, each bearing a 1 g promise. At 'Fully backed', frame this as the fully backed example. At '1 gram और', add one gold unit to the reserve; an arrow then enables issuance of note eleven.

beats.idea: Reserves support the gold promise
beats.shows: Vault gold linked to note’s promise receipt
beats.template_note: Defines reserved gold and backing; no transfer occurs.

beats.idea: Gold backs issue and qualified redemption
beats.shows: Reserve-backed notes issued; notes return for gold
beats.template_note: First show reserves behind the bank as its official issues notes to a holder. Then the holder returns notes and receives a fixed gold amount. Label redemption 'in principle; unrestricted नहीं' without inventing a conversion rate.

beats.idea: Weaker repayment capacity undermines confidence
beats.shows: Capacity falls; trust breaks; holders demand gold
beats.template_note: Lower the repayment-capacity meter, break the trust link, then show note holders presenting notes and requesting gold; do not show successful redemption.

beats.idea: Promise, reserves, and constrained issue
beats.shows: Promise → reserves → reserve-bound notes; 1g example tag
beats.template_note: Conceptual dependency sequence, not a new transaction. Reveal promise, reserves and constrained issue in order; mark '1 gram: सिर्फ उदाहरण', not a conversion rule.

beats.idea: Issuing notes carries redemption responsibility
beats.shows: Issued note tethered to gold redemption promise
beats.template_note: Summarizes the obligation behind issue; does not enact another issuance or redemption.

book_pictures.title: A horizontal line links four chronological dots
A horizontal timeline connects four dots from left to right

beats.idea: Receipts introduce different monetary milestones
beats.shows: Goods beside receipt; question mark above receipt
beats.template_note: A hypothetical question, not an enacted acceptance transaction.

beats.idea: Deposited-value claims gain a state issuer
beats.shows: Tang receipt precedes Song note with government seal
beats.template_note: Historical milestones and issuer identity, not a narrated deposit transaction.

beats.idea: Compulsory acceptance precedes Sweden's banknotes
beats.shows: Refusal crossed note; stamped law; earlier Chinese milestones
beats.template_note: Recipient refuses the note at मना; at compulsory acceptance replace refusal with a stamped law beside it. Highlight 1275 before Sweden 1661 without implying Sweden began paper money worldwide.

beats.idea: Gold anchors differ from universal gold access
beats.shows: Money–gold links; official access versus crossed public counter
beats.template_note: Show institutional links, not an enacted redemption; no conversion quantity is specified.

beats.idea: Gold redemption ends at the shared endpoint
beats.shows: Gold link breaks; both timelines meet at 1971
beats.template_note: Animate the redemption connector breaking; converge both timelines on the shared 1971 endpoint.

beats.idea: Why accept notes without gold redemption?
beats.shows: Recipient considers note; crossed gold promise; question mark
beats.template_note: Acceptance remains an unanswered question; do not animate a confirming nod.

beats.idea: Claims, issuers, acceptance and backing evolve
beats.shows: Receipt, issuer seal, acceptance law, broken gold link
beats.template_note: Recap historical changes through sequential highlights, not a fresh acceptance transaction.

beats.idea: Acceptance rests on trust in spending again
beats.shows: Note accepted; thought bubble shows spending it again
beats.template_note: Buyer offers ₹100 for rice; shopkeeper looks, nods, and a tick appears on स्वीकार. On भरोसा, a thought bubble shows the shopkeeper offering that same note to another seller for goods.

beats.idea: Authority and trust give fiat money value
beats.shows: Authority and trust support tomorrow’s grocery purchase
beats.template_note: Government seal and trusting public point toward the note. Cross only the paper-material source arrow on 'नहीं', not the note. On 'आज', buyer holds the note; calendar advances on 'कल'; buyer hands it to the shopkeeper, who hands back groceries.

beats.idea: Gold-backed paper is not necessarily fiat
beats.shows: Paper notes: gold redemption versus authority and trust
beats.template_note: Redemption names the historical basis rather than narrating a transaction. Show matched note slots: gold-backed note linked to gold by a redemption receipt; fiat note linked to government seal and trusting public. Cross an equals sign between generic paper money and fiat on 'नहीं'.

beats.idea: How is issuance controlled without gold?
beats.shows: Note issuance control questioned without gold backing
beats.template_note: Issuance control is only previewed. Retain authority and public-trust symbols; show gold outside the backing connection and place a question mark beside the note stack. Do not depict a control mechanism yet.

book_pictures.title: Major Examples of Fiat Currency Today

beats.idea: Fiat value rests on authority and trust
beats.shows: Press versus issuance; authority and trust support money
beats.template_note: Printing and issuance are posed as a distinction; their process follows in b24. Cross out a gold-silver backing link, not the metals themselves.

beats.idea: Printing is not authorised circulation
beats.shows: Printed notes await approval; replacement leaves total unchanged
beats.template_note: Press produces notes; authorisation gate releases them into circulation. In a separate replacement loop, equal-value old notes leave as new notes enter; total stays fixed.

beats.idea: Credit conditions affect demand with a lag
beats.shows: Costlier credit slows expansion, spending and price pressure
beats.template_note: Policy-rate and liquidity controls raise loan cost; shopkeeper pauses expansion, borrowing and spending shrink, then price pressure may ease after a clock delay. Reverse the demand arrows for cheaper credit; goods shelf does not refill.

beats.idea: Symbols and codes identify dollar and euro
beats.shows: USD marks America; EUR links participating EU countries
beats.template_note: Static location and currency identification; reserve vaults and trade arrows indicate USD's broad role without numerical shares.

beats.idea: Codes distinguish two yen-symbol currencies
beats.shows: Identical ¥ tags separate into JPY and CNY
beats.template_note: Matched slots show flag, code and role. JPY gets a stability shield, not a flat exchange-rate line; CNY gets trade and foreign-reserve assets.

beats.idea: An old currency name is not continuous fiat
beats.shows: Pound timeline separates ancient roots from modern fiat
beats.template_note: Historical timeline, not a transaction: mark 8th-century roots and today's fiat status; an intervening gold-promise receipt prevents implying uninterrupted fiat.

beats.idea: Historical Euro adoption was not universal
beats.shows: Twenty euro badges among twenty-seven historical EU tiles
beats.template_note: Show 27 member tiles, add euro badges to exactly 20 and leave seven unbadged. Keep 'Historical—not current' visible throughout.

beats.idea: Descriptions do not establish shares or fixed rates
beats.shows: Unsupported shares, fixed rates and rankings crossed out
beats.template_note: These are rejected inferences, not a person's refusal. Reveal each diagram before crossing its unsupported claim; leave Euro's ranking podium with a measure question mark and the old-name timeline broken before fiat.

beats.idea: More money cannot substitute for goods
beats.shows: Money grows; unchanged goods yield smaller purchasing basket
beats.template_note: First cross the equivalence link between reserve holdings and backing. Then grow money and demand against unchanged goods; if demand exceeds supply, show the same money buying fewer goods, labelled as possible rather than inevitable.

beats.idea: Valid payment extinguishes the debt
beats.relation_note: Acceptance of ₹100 clears the separate outstanding-debt counter.
beats.shows: ₹100 handed over; debt counter reaches ₹0
beats.template_note: Customer gives the valid ₹100 note; shopkeeper takes it and the debt ledger changes from ₹100 to ₹0.

beats.idea: Special-design valid coins also pay
beats.relation_note: The coin's special design does not prevent settlement of the ₹10 price.
beats.shows: Special-design ₹10 coin exchanged for ₹10 goods
beats.image_wanted: Indian circulating commemorative ₹10 coin obverse reverse
beats.template_note: Customer hands one ₹10 coin to the shopkeeper; shopkeeper accepts it and hands over the ₹10 goods.

beats.idea: Notes unlimited; coin acceptance has a limit
beats.relation_note: Contrast growing banknote payments with a ₹1,000 compulsory-acceptance line for ₹10 coins; above it acceptance is voluntary.
beats.shows: Notes grow; coin meter stops; extra coin optional
beats.template_note: First hand over two ₹500 notes against ₹1,000, then three against ₹1,500, without a ceiling mark. Count 100 ₹10 coins as the meter reaches its red ₹1,000 line. Hold the 101st coin outside the compulsory stack: total offered ₹1,010, extra acceptance labelled मर्ज़ी. Do not cross out the valid extra coin.

beats.idea: Official recognition and everyday circulation
beats.relation_note: Recognition applies within the government's territory; a second vignette illustrates circulation commemorative coins.
beats.shows: Recognised money inside India; commemorative coin buys goods
beats.template_note: Within the territory outline, a payer hands recognised money to a recipient; at 'Circulation commemorative coins', a commemorative coin similarly pays for goods.

beats.idea: Valid banknotes have no total tender ceiling
beats.relation_note: Contrast an indefinitely extending banknote stack with the absence of a stopping line; this concerns tender amount, not transaction permissions.
nouns: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 law scroll
beats.shows: Valid note stacks grow without a ceiling
beats.template_note: Banknotes join a growing stack; its amount meter keeps extending without a stop line. Reveal the six denominations as named, then the stamped RBI Act scroll.

beats.idea: Compulsory coin acceptance stops at a limit
beats.relation_note: The line limits compulsory acceptance, not coin validity; acceptance beyond it remains voluntary.
beats.shows: Coin meter stops; extra coins await choice
beats.template_note: Coins accumulate until the meter reaches a red 'कानूनी सीमा' line. Keep additional valid coins outside the compulsory-acceptance zone beside the recipient's choice symbol; show the stamped Coinage Act scroll.

beats.idea: Tender status is not unrestricted cash use
beats.relation_note: Three paired contrasts separate tender ceiling from transaction permission, special design from circulation evidence, and acceptance limits from validity.
beats.shows: Cash barrier; collector case; over-limit coins retain ticks
beats.template_note: These are conceptual contrasts, not a counting process: show transaction restrictions separately, no automatic circulation tick from design alone, and validity ticks remaining on coins beyond the acceptance line.

beats.idea: Recognition first, then denomination and total limit
beats.relation_note: After recognition, compare notes and coins using matching denomination and total-amount slots.
beats.shows: Recognised notes extend; recognised coins meet limit
beats.template_note: A question mark beside recognised money resolves into paired note and coin diagrams: denomination labels above, an open-ended note meter and a capped coin meter below. No counting action is narrated.

beats.idea: Legal tender need not always be fiat
beats.shows: Fiat and Bitcoin beside crossed universal rule

beats.idea: Commemorative coins have distinct status and values
beats.shows: Coin group: mostly legal; metal and collector branches
beats.template_note: Payment is questioned, not enacted; the visual classifies coins without inventing a transaction.

beats.idea: Collector sets are preserved rather than routinely spent
beats.shows: Mint sets enter collection; faint branch toward shopping
beats.image_wanted: Government Mint commemorative proof coin set UNC coin set protective presentation packaging
beats.template_note: Mint seller hands a packaged set to a collector; inset distinguishes reflective proof finish from UNC, labelled Uncirculated. Collector keeps the set protected; a faint shopping branch indicates rare use, not prohibition.

beats.idea: अमान्य coins से बकाया नहीं मिटता
beats.relation_note: एक ही ₹1 bill के दो विकल्प: पुराने चार 25 paise coins अस्वीकृत, बकाया ₹1; valid ₹1 coin स्वीकार, बकाया ₹0। अंत में पुराने coins के legal-tender stamp को काटें।
beats.shows: चार पुराने coins अस्वीकृत; valid coin स्वीकार, बकाया शून्य
beats.template_note: चार पुराने coins पेश करें; दुकानदार मना करे, cross लगे और ₹1 बाकी रहे। valid ₹1 coin पेश करने पर nod और tick आएँ, बकाया ₹0 हो। demonetization पर पुराने coins का legal-tender stamp कटे।

beats.idea: Coin groups की अलग tender limits
beats.relation_note: तीन पंक्तियाँ: ₹1/₹2/₹5/₹10/₹20 का साझा meter ₹1,000 पर रुके; 50 paise का अलग meter ₹10 पर रुके; छोटे coins पर cross, कोई valid-payment meter नहीं।
beats.shows: Coin groups; ₹1,000 और ₹10 meters; छोटे coins crossed
beats.template_note: डिब्बे के coins तीन groups में खुलें। पहले group के coins गिरने पर साझा meter ₹1,000 की red line तक; 50 paise coins का meter ₹10 तक। छोटे coins पर cross लगाएँ, payment total में न जोड़ें।

book_pictures.title: Current legal limits for coins (Coinage Act, 2011)

beats.idea: Limits measure value, not coin count
beats.shows: Two coin piles fill separate rupee-limit meters
beats.template_note: Count 50 ₹20 coins as the value meter reaches ₹1,000; keep count 50 separate from the ₹1,000 red line. Cross out the mistaken label ‘1,000 coins’ at ‘नहीं’. Then count 20 fifty-paise coins to the ₹10 red line. Show denomination × count beside each pile.

beats.idea: Different denominations have different status
beats.shows: Separated coins: value limit versus withdrawn status
beats.template_note: Move 50-paise and 25-paise coins from a box into matching comparison slots. Give 50 paise a ₹10 limit marker; cross the 25-paise legal-tender badge at ‘नहीं’. Then show a commemorative coin with a status question mark; cross ‘सभी’ at ‘नहीं’ and leave its numerical count unknown.

beats.idea: Payment limit and collector price do not change status
beats.shows: Limit exceeded; status unchanged; collector tag powerless
beats.template_note: Left: a valid-denomination pile passes the ₹1,000 line while its legal-tender status badge remains unchanged. Right: attach a collector-price tag to the withdrawn 25-paise coin; its crossed legal-tender badge remains crossed. Do not depict change being returned.

beats.idea: Calculate value, then check limit and status
beats.shows: Coin value calculation leads to two checks
beats.template_note: Reveal denomination coin × counted stack, producing total rupee value. Arrow to a comparison with the table’s total-value limit, then arrow to a separate legal-tender-status check. Number the three stages.

beats.idea: Bitcoin payment does not prove government issuance
beats.shows: Phone Bitcoin; government issuer questioned, then crossed
beats.template_note: Payment is a visual premise, not a narrated transaction.

beats.idea: Legal tender exception with non-government creation and pricing
beats.shows: 2024 recognition; network creates Bitcoin; market sets price
beats.template_note: Network-rule mining produces Bitcoin; demand and supply move its price; cross the government fixed-value promise.

beats.idea: 2025 removes compulsion, not voluntary use
beats.shows: Compulsion crossed; wallet ticked; willing parties exchange Bitcoin
beats.template_note: Remove the compulsory stamp; retain ownership tick; buyer and seller both nod before phone-to-phone Bitcoin transfer.

beats.idea: Recognition changes without changing the issuer
beats.shows: Changed law scrolls above identical Bitcoin networks
beats.template_note: Compare legal status across dates while keeping the issuance network unchanged.

beats.idea: Ask three separate monetary-status questions
beats.shows: Network, wallet, handshake and compulsory stamp questioned separately
beats.template_note: Acceptance is a diagnostic category here, not an acceptance action.

beats.idea: One coin, two roles
beats.shows: Same coin, payment versus collection, price question mark
beats.template_note: Hypothetical valuation question, not a narrated transaction.

beats.idea: Face value differs from market price
beats.shows: Matching coins: ₹100 payment, several-thousand collector price
beats.template_note: Compares values without enacting a sale.

beats.idea: Collector premium leaves denomination unchanged
beats.shows: Silver, condition, collectability drive premium; ₹100 stays
beats.template_note: Collector hands premium payment to seller; silver, condition and collectability icons explain it. Keep denomination fixed at ₹100.

beats.idea: Collector price is not a legal payment measure
beats.shows: Collector price unequal to debt amount or limit
beats.template_note: Rejects equivalence, not a payment; show crossed equality links to debt receipt and legal-limit meter, without an invented limit.

beats.idea: Use the value appropriate to the role
beats.shows: Payment coin denomination; collection mutually agreed price
beats.template_note: Summary comparison; no transaction is enacted.

beats.idea: Cheque transfers existing deposits, subject to funds
beats.shows: Cheque clears; college gains ₹1,000, student retains ₹1,000
beats.template_note: Open with a fee bill and cash-free question mark. Write a ₹1,000 instruction, hand it to the bank, then show clearing: student deposit ₹2,000 to ₹1,000 and college receipt +₹1,000. At 'Funds कम', branch to insufficient funds, no completed transfer and fees still due; do not invent a shortfall amount.

beats.idea: Credit payment creates repayment debt
beats.shows: Issuer pays college; student debt rises to ₹1,000
beats.template_note: Animate issuer-to-college payment of ₹1,000. Student's debt to issuer changes from ₹0 to ₹1,000, excluding charges; add a student-to-issuer repayment arrow marked due, not paid. Keep the deposit account separate and undebited to distinguish credit from deposited money.

beats.idea: Payment instruments do not confer currency status
beats.shows: Cheque accesses deposits; card accesses credit; status separate
beats.template_note: Payment and acceptance are discussed conceptually; no transaction is narrated. Match cheque and card slots: deposit instruction versus credit access. College acceptance gets a tick, but an arrow from acceptance to fiat/legal-tender status is crossed out.

beats.idea: Separate dimensions; dollar demand remains a question
beats.shows: Three separate dimensions; unlinked dollar, gold, demand question
beats.template_note: First show separate value, legal-status and payment-method groups. At 'gold link' reveal gold and dollar with a broken link; at 'क्यों' add a question mark beside demand arrows pointing toward the dollar.
